newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban "satisfied" with Dostum talks.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban "satisfied" with Dostum talks.

text.p: The Taleban authorities in Kabul said on Thursday they had been assured by northern Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum that he would not join in the fighting north of the Afghan capital.

"He has assured us," acting information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told Reuters after reports surfaced that Dostum had sent forces south to join those of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
"If he does join in the fighting, it will be his decision," Mutaqi said without elaboration.
On Wednesday, Taleban Foreign Minister Mulla Mohammed Ghous held talks with Dostum, who has perhaps the most potent single armed force in Afghanistan.
Mutaqi said the Taleban were satisfied with the talks and that a Dostum delegation would soon visit Kandahar, the southern city where the Taleban have their headquarters, for further negotiations.
He said one aim of the talks "was to persuade the northern movement not to make friendship with those forces who have been expelled and isolated by the people", a reference to Masood.

"About this issue, the northern movement has given us assurances. We are satisfied with them. We will have nore talks in this regard and our concern is to a great degree about Dostum's involvement in the fighting," Mutaqi said.
Shortly before he spoke, Dostum General Abdul Majid Ruzi told reporters in Jabal os-Siraj at the mouth of the Salang Pass through the Hindu Kush mountains that Uzbek forces were being sent south.

"As you know, the (Afghan Defence) Council decided that if there was an attack, all the forces would come together and we would insert our troops and our tanks and our artillery into the line and we have," Ruzi said.
Uzbek forces were heading south of Jabal os-Siraj towards the town of Charikar, a 30-minute drive south and just north of the front line between the Taleban and Masood's forces.
"We came from the Salang and we're going to Kabul. We're going to bash the Taleban today," said one Uzbek soldier on the way south.
